report: Patient has sudden ascending paralysis with intact sensation, triggered by corticosteroid injection and high-carbohydrate meal. Labs show potassium 1.9 mmol/L, suppressed TSH, elevated free T4, and elevated TSH receptor antibody, confirming thyrotoxicosis. Rapid resolution after IV potassium and preserved sensation rule out Guillain-Barré syndrome and acute myelopathy. The graph links these findings to thyrotoxic periodic paralysis, a subtype of hypokalemic periodic paralysis, diagnostic.
